messages:
anya: Heads up — after the KV paging defrag patch landed on staging I'm seeing tail-latency spikes on long chat sessions (seq 4k+). Not constant but frequent during mixed-size batches.
kevin: Can you paste the profiler trace? is this before or after we switched the FlashAttn fallback path?
anya: After. Traces attached below show a lot of time in `block_table::alloc` and `kv_pager::evict_page`. Sample snippet: 
```
# perf top-ish
samples  pcnt  symbol
420     34%   block_table::alloc_block
210     17%   kv_pager::evict_page
90      7%    flash_attn_fallback_kernel
...
```
mike: hmm that looks like fragmentation churn. The defrag pass is coalescing holes synchronously on alloc, right?
anya: Yeah — current strategy: try fast-fit free-list, if failed trigger defrag which scans neighbor blocks and moves live KV entries to coalesce. We expected moves to be rare.
sophia: Do we have numbers on move cost? Especially with fused attention kernels where token memcpy cost competes with kernel overhead.
anya: Measured on p4d: moving one 128xKV slice ~ 0.45ms (host memcpy + device copies + metadata). When the defrag loop hits many small holes it does dozens per batch.
kevin: That explains tail spikes. Two quick ideas: 1) switch to a background async defrag worker, 2) change allocation to a segmented free-list (small/medium/large) to reduce defrag hits.
mike: Also consider an age-separated LRU: never move very recent KV entries (hot tokens) to avoid churn; only compact cold regions during low load.
sophia: For background defrag: need to ensure we don't block kernel selection for the request that's waiting. Batching heuristics expect immediate alloc success to decide whether to pick FlashAttn or fallback. If alloc is async, the runtime might pick a fallback kernel prematurely.
kevin: Good point. Maybe expose a fast-path soft-reserve: if alloc fails synchronously, and a background compaction is underway, allow a tiny retry window (1-2ms) before switching kernel. That lets short defrags finish and keeps FlashAttn for most cases.
anya: I ran an experiment: added 2ms spin retry + background defrag. Result: P99 reduced from 210ms -> 120ms for 4k sequences, but CPU usage spiked on control-plane threads.
kevin: Can you share the micro-benchmark harness? bench-bot what do you have from the last run?
bench-bot: Summary: workload=chat-mix, batch-size=8, seq=4096, 50k requests. Baselines: old alloc=no-defrag, new alloc=sync-defrag, new2=bg-defrag+2ms-retry.
```
baseline (no-defrag): P50 45ms P95 88ms P99 160ms
sync-defrag:        P50 48ms P95 130ms P99 210ms
bg-defrag+2ms:      P50 46ms P95 92ms  P99 120ms
cpu ctrl threads %user: baseline 24% -> bg-defrag 46%
```
mike: That looks promising but we can't double control-plane CPU. Maybe throttle defrag worker concurrency and avoid copying hot KV slices. Add heuristics: only move blocks with occupancy < 30% or age > 5000ms.
sophia: Another angle: change block table allocation unit to prefer power-of-two sized buckets so kernel memory access patterns stay aligned for FlashAttn. Fragmented non-aligned blocks could slow fused kernels.
kevin: Agree. Also ensure kernel selection heuristics consider expected fragmentation penalty. We can add a cheap estimator: if free_small_blocks / total_blocks > 0.4 then prefer fallback kernels since packed small holes harm FlashAttn throughput.
anya: Quick pseudo for eviction policy we discussed: 
```
# evict_policy(pages_needed):
  candidates = free_list.find_candidates(pages_needed)
  if candidates: return alloc_from(candidates)
  if background_defrag.running: sleep(0.001..0.002) and retry
  # prefer cold/coalescable spans
  spans = block_table.scan(low_occupancy=true, age>5s)
  pick = best_coalesce(spans)
  evict(pick)
  return alloc_from(pick)
```
kevin: We should also instrument a fragmentation metric exposed to the console: percent_holes, avg_hole_size, largest_hole. That'll help correlate with kernel selection logs.
anya: Added logging patch to staging: `kv.fragmentation.{pct_holes,avg_size,max_size}`. Early runs show pct_holes spikes right before P99 jumps.
kevin: For rollout plan: I propose bg-defrag default off, opt-in via runtime flag. Also implement throttling + occupancy thresholds. We'll run A/B on dedicated pool.
mike: Agreed. I'll prototype segregated free-lists (tiny: <=4 pages, small: <=16, large: >16) and avoid moving tiny allocations.
sophia: One more: when we pick a fallback kernel due to allocation uncertainty, tag the request so we can do post-request re-eval to try to switch back to FlashAttn for next batch. Adds some adaptive learning.
anya: Nice. I'll open PRs: one for bg-defrag + metrics, one for segmented free-lists, one for allocator heuristics. Tagging @kevin @mike for review.
kevin: Thanks. Can we capture a short checklist for the PRs?
mike: checklist: 1) unit tests for hole coalescing 2) perf microbench harness update 3) dashboard metrics 4) flag gating + default off 5) docs for kernel-selection heuristic param
sophia: I'll add a tracing span for alloc+evict so we can correlate per-request kernel picks with allocator latency.
anya: Cool. I'll drop follow-up logs after first bg-defrag run tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
